utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The court is in session. Registrar, can you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar. Today is Tuesday, 26th of January, 2010. I would like to welcome the accused who are present, Defence counsel, Mr. Kruger, Mr. Stringer, and their associates, as well as the witness and all the people assisting us. Before I give the floor to Mr. Kruger, Colonel, I'd like to get back to an issue which has been discussed yesterday already and which I'm concerned about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We saw a document yesterday which referred to the fact that you belonged to the Croatian Army. I mentioned to you yesterday that this document had varying pages with different fonts. I could infer thereof that the Prosecution's exhibit is a compilation of various reports. That is a possibility, but not a certainty. You may know or you may not know that the OTP, a few years ago, made requests for assistance to the Republic of Croatia for the latter to hand over any information they had to the OTP. The document we have is a 1996 document. I believe that is the case, and I believe it is the answer to a request made by the OTP to the Croatian authorities at the time, asking to have the full list of all Croatian officers who had been part of the HVO. The authorities of your country, therefore, sent this document in reply. Since I do not have the request made by the OTP, this is where the ambiguity lies. Did the Prosecution ask to have the full list of all the officers that had been members of the HVO if no specific date had been given? This may, therefore, have included officers who were officers in the Croatian Army and then officers in the HVO, who then may have returned to the Croatian Army, or officers like you who were part of the HVO and who joined the Croatian Army afterwards. So we have several cases. You are testifying under oath, which means that you are not entitled to make a false testimony. I must, therefore, also consider the possibility that you were, first of all, a member of the Croatian Army and then a member of the HVO. This is a theoretical assumption I'm making. But if that is the case, I would also consider the situation where the Prosecution might be wanting to go into this in detail and, therefore, ask the Croatian authorities to disclose anything concerning you. And if, at a closer look at your file, it appears that as of 1992 you were a member of the Croatian Army, and not in August 1993, the Prosecutor could then issue an indictment against you. I anticipate all problems. That is my role as a Judge, and I feel I have the duty today to ask you, once again, to make sure we can settle this issue. I want you to tell us whether, when you joined the Croatian Army in August 1993, you did not draft a document stating that you were already a member of the Croatian Army, because sometimes the administration can make mistakes, mistakes which could be due to you or which could be due to the personnel or people who recruited you in the Croatian Army, because any mistake does have consequences. You may or you may not have lied. Please, can you confirm that when you left the HVO in August 1993, you incorporated the Croatian Army, you asked to be integrated into the Croatian Army, but prior to that you had never been paid by the Croatian Army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, Your Honour, I can confirm that I was never previously paid by the Croatian Army. So if it takes 20 years for one to be pensioned off, this period starts for me from the 5th of August, 1994. That was the date when I started working and signed a contract with the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are telling us the 5th of August, 1994. What did you do between August 1993 and the 5th of August, 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was in training at the Croatian Military School.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you were training at the Croatian Military School, were you then being paid by the Croatian Army or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All students were paid at the time through the Croatian Military School, all the students of the Croatian Military School.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll finish off with a question. It's a shame that General Praljak is not here today. He's ill, unfortunately, but his lawyers will certainly forward the question. In August 1993, before leaving, you were still an analyst working for the VOS within the Main Staff. We know that General Praljak took up his position at the end of July 1993, which would mean that when General Praljak took up his command, you were still there for a few days. It wasn't a matter of weeks, but it was a matter of days. When you left the VOS, did you then ask General Praljak for the permission to leave, or did you just tell him that you had enrolled at the Military School and that you were going to leave, just giving him the bare facts ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, at that time towards the end of August and one part of the month of July, I was on the payroll of the VOS, and I was working in Sector North. And I left to be trained upon the proposal by my chief and by General Praljak, which means that General Praljak was aware of my leaving for training.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're saying that General Praljak knew that you were going to go on training. Well, that, at least, is very clear. Thank you for your answers, which are very clear. During the night, a few questions came to mind, and I felt I had the duty to put these questions to you. Mr. Kruger, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, and good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Mr. Jasak, good morning to you, too. Now, sir, last night we tried to look at a video and we had some technical problems, so let's start this morning by looking --

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's start by looking at the video of a very small part of the meeting between General Petkovic and Commander Sefer Halilovic, and this is the meeting which you said last night that you were not present at. And this takes place early in May 1993. If we could just play the video. Sorry, for the record, it's Exhibit P02187, and we are looking at a segment from 5 minutes and 27 seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "This should be a conversation between us, the representatives of the army and the representatives of the HVO. You may be present, but this talk is more an internal talk. At this gathering imposing as to the number of participants as well as to the number of functions of the people present here, we want at last a final answer. Are we allies or are we enemies? If we are, indeed, allies, then we have to know that and behave accordingly. And if we are enemies, then we have to know that as well and behave accordingly. But we will not disarm people in Central Bosnia and in Mostar, arrest them, drag people out of their homes, and do all those things that are being done while we are holding talks and establishing joint commands. And while establishing joint commands, we won't have convoys with humanitarian aid and other convoys. It is known to the gentlemen to which convoys I'm referring, standing still in Central Bosnia and Herzegovina, standing where they shouldn't be, there where they should not stand, while at the same time in Gorazde and in Eastern Bosnia and in Srebrenica and in North-Eastern Bosnia, people are dying of hunger, dying because they do not have arms. And you may not hold a convoy as you did two days ago, arrest five clerics, seize 200.000 weapons, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Now, sir, at this stage when this meeting took place, and it's late in May, if I'm not mistaken, it's not the 4th of May -- this takes place sometime after the 9th of May; would you agree?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, objection to this question. How should the witness know when this was recorded?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I think the witness can say that, that he does not know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, I don't think so. It is not fair towards the witness. We know how this film has been marked. It has been marked as something that was taken on the 4th of May in Jablanica. We've seen it a lot of times in this courtroom. There are no dilemmas here, and I don't know what the foundation may be for this question to be connected with the 9th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I personally don't believe that the Prosecutor tried to confuse the witness intentionally. However, we have information about the evidence, and it has been said about this film that we've already seen that this meeting took place on the 4th of May. So if my learned friend is putting the film to the witness, he has to start from the fair facts or otherwise he's trying to set a trap for the witness, which I sincerely doubt that he is doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I won't belabour the exact date of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: What I will ask, sir, is: In May 1993, it's correct that the ABiH and the HVO were still allies against the Serbs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when this film was recorded. However, in May 1993 the BiH Army and the HVO were allies against the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: And, sir, my next question is, then: If we assume -- if we accept that this meeting took place in May 1993, can you tell the Court what has the HVO done which would cause Mr. Halilovic to ask this question, Are we friends or are we allies? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I object to the form of the question. First of all, we don't know whether Halilovic is telling the truth and whether he's just saying this for the purposes of the camera and those who are there to witness the events. So I think it assumes a fact, first of all, which certainly has not been proved. And also the gentleman indicated -- in fact, it was Mr. Kruger who started by saying, I know you were not there. So if he wasn't there, how can he then begin to pose questions about the meeting to which he wasn't present at?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to add something to that. My learned friend says, before putting the question, We're not going to dwell upon dates. I would like to remind you that this is P2187, and on page 1 of the English transcript it says that the date is 4 May 1993. The question is whether the Prosecutor doubts his own evidence. Does the Prosecutor want to confuse us by claiming that something, in this particular case this piece of evidence, was recorded on the 4th of May, 1993, and then they change their mind and say, Maybe not? How can we prepare our case on that? We start from the point that what the Prosecutor has given us is probably true, but when the Prosecutor doubts his own evidence, I really don't know what we are all doing in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kruger, this video so far is dated the 4th of May, 1993. If you agree that it is on the 4th of May, 1993, you then settle the issue, knowing that, of course, the witness cannot answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Witness, indeed, I accept that it's the 4th of May. The mistake is entirely mine. I was listening to the clip, and just one part of the clip certainly triggered my mind and set it off at a tangent. Your Honour, but as to the objection by Ms. Alaburic, Your Honour, I simply can't agree -- or, sorry, by Mr. Karnavas. The witness was an intelligence analyst, and certainly this is a question which he's entitled -- or fully entitled to answer. He was receiving intelligence reports, and certainly he would know from his intelligence notes if there was anything which could justify a question such as this by Mr. Halilovic on the 4th of May. And further, Your Honour, if there's also an objection as to the foundation for asking this question, then certainly most of the testimony that he was giving -- that he gave last week is also evidence that should then not have been heard, because certainly there was then no foundation for that evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Put your questions. I will have a question after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you have heard that Mr. Halilovic says or asks to Mr. Petkovic, General Petkovic, Are we friends or are we enemies? Now, sir, can you tell the Court, do you know of anything which may have justified General Halilovic asking such a question of General Petkovic at this time?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know about the date 4th of May, and it was my colleague Dinko Zebic who told me about that meeting, that meeting was very skillfully used by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina as a propaganda tool. Nobody was allowed to visit Croatian villages, most of which had been burned by that time. This means that the media and the journalists were used to dispatch something that was nothing short of a propaganda material.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you still haven't answered the question. Were you aware of anything which may have caused General Halilovic to ask this question? And if I may ask you, sir, please do not look at General Petkovic for approval. I see you constantly looking at General Petkovic and looking for approval, and then General Petkovic nods to you. Please don't do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I really object to this remark by my learned friend Kruger, and I must admit that I don't see what is happening behind my back, but I'm absolutely certain that General Petkovic is not giving any signs to the witness, nor that this witness needs to look at anybody in order to be given a signal as to how to answer. So I'm saying this remark as the Prosecutor's attempt to discredit the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just one sentence, if I may. In our circles in Croatia, our legal circles in Croatia, we call it poisoning the record. You just throw something and then it is recorded, and when the Appeals Chamber reads it, they base their judgement on that. This is a lie which has nothing whatsoever to do with the reality. I've been watching the witness for four days now, and the witness, when he answers, does, indeed, look all over the courtroom, but that's not to say that he is asking approval from either General Petkovic or anybody else. This should not be allowed because it doesn't hold water, and I'm sure that if this, indeed, was the case, you would have noticed that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, the Prosecutor put a very specific question to you. Please answer that question now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I've already answered, and I said that that meeting was nothing short of propaganda by General Halilovic. That's how I heard it from my colleague Dinko Zebic. That meeting followed after major conflicts when most of the Croatian villages had already been burned, people had been killed or expelled or were fully encircled. That is the time-frame, and that was around Konjic, and that was nothing but propaganda.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Let's have a look at a next clip from this same video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. Before we look at the next video-clip: Sir, this is a video we've seen already, and it doesn't come as a surprise for us Judges. There is, however, a third component here, which is a new one; i.e., the Spaniards. The Spaniards are neutral, and under their aegis a meeting is organised between General Halilovic and General Petkovic. And we realise that General Halilovic puts the question, which is a fundamental question, Are we allies or enemies? This is a topic which you addressed last week, since you said that they were neighbours and a neighbour is a friend. Therefore, there was a foundation to the question. Since you brought this up last week, and General Halilovic turns to his counterpart and says, Are we allies or enemies, and he did this in the presence of the Spaniards, which means, in my view, that on the 4th of May there is the HVO and the ABiH that are united, and the issue of a joint command is definitely on the agenda, since it was raised at the meeting. If they were enemies in the classic sense of the term, I would find it difficult to imagine that a high-ranking Spanish officer would convene a meeting between enemies. He would thus run the risk of people bringing out their weapons at the meeting and people getting killed. I assume that the Spaniard did take a number of precautions. He would have not run the risk of convening a meeting between enemies. This is something which I certainly take into account. You did not attend this meeting, but as Mr. Kruger said, since you were an analyst, you might have had some information about it, about the reason behind the question. We have no specific answer from General Petkovic, because as we can see, the question of the humanitarian aid will be raised, the fact that there were blockades, and so on. Maybe that was the reason, but maybe there were other reasons. In other words, all the incidents that occurred before that, and what I think of as Hamzici and Trusina and other villages. Perhaps General Halilovic, who together with General Petkovic had been involved in the negotiations in Geneva, perhaps he wants to fulfill his role to the full, maybe, also. According to you, if General Halilovic puts this question, it is due to skirmishes that occurred before. The mere fact that they share a common enemy, i.e., the Serbs, that doesn't preclude the fact that there might be skirmishes between the two. And since you were a VOS analyst, you might be able to answer this question, or, as you say, it's just a question of propaganda.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if we're dealing with the 4th of May, that date, this is just a segment. I received information from my colleague that the whole event was made use of as promotion, as a propaganda, and that the goal was to resolve the problems of the Croatian villages in the area and the captured. And from the 18th of April, we have an agreement between Boban and Izetbegovic. We have an agreement on the 20th between General Petkovic and Halilovic. But we also have, after that, orders issued by the BH Army for attack, and we also have information from the Intelligence Service, from around the 23rd of April, I believe, that the Croatian villages which were in the area were either set fire to and the population expelled or that they were under siege. So that was the situation that came before. But at that meeting, to the best of my knowledge, they were supposed to agree to tour those villages. And according to my information, I don't think that was ever done. So this means that it was just used as propaganda by the BH Army, that particular meeting. I don't know the details of it, of course. I'm just speaking about the meeting based on the information that I had received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So according to you, what Halilovic is saying is that he is speaking as part of a propaganda. Mr. Kruger, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Just to follow up on this, sir: In April, therefore, you were aware of certain conflicts which had taken place between the ABiH and the HVO?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had information about what happened in April, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: And even before that? Did you have information about conflicts in January and in October the previous year?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything that happened until the 23rd of March, 1993, was dealt with on a daily basis. So the more serious conflicts began on the 23rd of March, 1993, in the Konjic area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, had the HVO done anything to cause those conflicts or contributed to causing those conflicts?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, the HVO did not do anything to cause those conflicts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not going to show you the second clip. The second clip dealt only with, once again, General Halilovic saying to Mr. Petkovic that, Mostar will never be only Croat. All that I'll ask you about that is: Were you aware that the ABiH and the Muslims in Herceg-Bosna were not supportive of the idea of a Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. The BH Army and the Muslims in Herceg-Bosna, that they did not support the idea of Herceg-Bosna? What? Is that what you asked?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Did the Muslims and -- or let's say the Muslims within the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, who lived within that area, are you aware that they were not supportive of the idea of the establishment of that Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Muslims who lived on this territory under the control of the Croatian Defence Council were on a footing of equality with the Croats in the Croatian Defence Council, so automatically they supported the idea. Otherwise, they didn't have to be in the Croatian Defence Council. Nobody forced them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Sir, let's move on. Let's look at Exhibit P01911, and this is in binder 2. It's Exhibit P01911. Now, sir, this document is a document from the ECMM, and it's dated the 16th of April, 1993, and it's a political and military analysis about the present Jablanica crisis. Now, the first thing that I'd like to refer you to is paragraph 2 or section 2, which is titled "Regional Importance," and there it says, first paragraph: "The region immediately north of Bugojno, Gornji Vakuf, Prozor, Jablanica, Konjic Road is predominantly Muslim, yet under the Vance-Owen Plan is due to fall under the control of Provinces 8 and 10. The HVO signed the plan and have expressed a strong desire to implement the plan." Sir, you are aware of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that a Vance-Owen Peace Plan existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: And you don't disagree with what is stated here, that these provinces would fall within Provinces 8 and 10, which would fall under -- that these provinces would fall under -- that these municipalities would fall under Provinces 8 and 10; you don't disagree with that, do you?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see here, what it says, at least in the Croatian version, that this is a document dated the 17th of April, and as far as I know, the overall Vance-Owen Plan, the complete plan, was signed by Alija Izetbegovic and Mate Boban with all the attachments and supplements much before this. I think it was in March, the 25th of March, I think, 1993. So I don't see that the problem here was that there was a strong intention on the HVO and BH Army to -- I don't see that there was any problem in them implementing it. If the leaders of the two nations signed it, I don't see the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Sir, you haven't answered the question. Is it correct that these provinces fell within -- or these municipalities mentioned here fell within Provinces 8 and 10?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they were municipalities under Provinces 8 and 10, Jablanica, Konjic, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: And Provinces 8 and 10 are provinces assigned to the Croats; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Provinces 8 and 10, well, yes, they're parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina, so they belong to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Sir, Provinces 8 and 10 were assigned to the Croats under the Vance-Owen Peace Plan? That's the question, and you don't disagree with that; that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I agree that they were regions where Croats lived and that they were in the majority there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Sir, your answer doesn't make sense. We're talking about Konjic, Jablanica, Gornji Vakuf. Those are definitely provinces or municipalities which are predominantly Muslim, yet these municipalities have been assigned, under the Vance-Owen Peace Plan, to Provinces 8 and 10. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, they were assigned, these Provinces 8 and 10, but there were other municipalities, too, not only those two in those provinces. So the provinces, if you look at them in their entirety, the Croats were the most numerous populous there, according to the 1991 census, that is to say, in those provinces. One province had its headquarters in Mostar, and the other one in Travnik, according to the Vance-Owen Plan, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: And, sir, the next part of the report says: "To the HVO, 'implementation' means 'taking control of,' with an emphasis on 'ownership' of the provinces rather than 'responsibility' for them." Is that correct, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what "ownership" is meant here. In private ownership, you know who the owner is, regardless of the province.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Sir, on the next page, just prior to section 3 on political activity, it says, and now we're referring to this region -- Jablanica region: "Indeed, the region is not just important, it is strategically vital both for military and economic reasons, not just in the history of Herceg-Bosna, but for its future prosperity and security." Is that a correct statement?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just allow me a moment to read this. Political activities, is that what you're referring to in point 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: No, it's -- sir, it's just prior to political activity, the last paragraph of the section dealing with regional importance. It's that last section. Is it correct that Jablanica --

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: "This region is not only important, but it is strategically vital both for military and economic reasons." But which region?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: This report deals with Jablanica, sir. This is the Jablanica region, sir.

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Jablanica is vital for the whole of Bosnia-Herzegovina, not only for this particular region.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Let's have a look at the political activity in paragraph 3 and what the ECMM is observing, or how they view the events. It says, the first paragraph: "The clashes that have occurred in the past months have generally followed provocation, and it is the experience of ECMM and some UNPROFOR units that the provocation is usually HVO inspired." Now, sir, if the internationals are saying this, do you know or do you have any idea on what basis or what has led them to believe that the HVO is actually the one provoking?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Meetings like the one held by Sefer Halilovic, that is to say, propaganda on the part of Bosnia-Herzegovina, probably that. I don't know what else. That they had very strong propaganda.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Didn't the HVO also have strong propaganda?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Let's look at the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that this deserves objection. [Interpretation] My dear colleague asked us to focus on paragraph 1 of point 3 of this document, and he put it to the witness -- he claimed that the ECMM was claiming and saying that the HVO, as it has been recorded in the transcript, and I'll quote, that the HVO is actually the one provoking. So the assertion is -- that was the assertion. And then the witness is responding. I'd like to draw your attention that that's not what the document says. The document says as follows: "The ECMM and some UNPROFOR units, that the provocation is usually HVO inspired." So obviously the author of this report does not have information about who was doing the provoking, but he started out from the assumption that the incidents or clashes or whatever took place because of -- caused by confrontation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry. "Caused by provocation," interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And then he writes the general observation that usually -- they are usually. So the ECMM is not saying who did the provocation, but they say, We think that it was usually inspired by the HVO. And on that basis, the Prosecutor is categorically stating that it was, indeed, the HVO who did the provoking and that that's what the document says. Once again, that is improper questioning, and he's trying to mislead the witness. The witness has been provided with the document, and he could have said, There's the extract, take a moment to read it, and may we have your comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: My comments and my fear go beyond this, because I'm watching also the expression of the Bench, and at least one of the members of the Bench is showing faces of incredulity at some of the answers, which leads me to believe that at least one member of the Bench believes everything that he reads in these reports as being true, accurate, and complete. Now, we have seen a great deal of propaganda on everyone's side. In particular, we have seen where, for instance, even today's vice-president of the United States was going around saying that, In Bosnia, we only have Bosnians who are Catholic, Orthodox, or Muslim, based on what he had been told by Silajdzic. And also we have documents that Alihodzic was saying the same things. And my concern is that now we're using this particular document to somehow validate what's in it. Now, I understand the technique. If Mr. Kruger wishes to show that this is what the ECMM is saying, especially when it gets to the word "usually," as was pointed out by Mr. Kovacic, then -- and if the gentleman then says, I don't know what you're talking about, it is up to Mr. Kruger then to demonstrate concretely, with correct and accurate facts, how it is that this ECMM report, or whoever he or she may be, has actually come up to this conclusion. In other words, we're using this and we're using vital time in this courtroom in order to somehow bolster the credibility of this particular report, and this is utterly improper, at least in an adversarial system which to this date this Tribunal still abides by.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you're a Defence witness, and the Prosecutor is asking you a question based on a document coming from a body of the international community; namely, the observers from the European Union. According to them, and it is relayed by the Prosecutor, the document seems to say - but I'm very cautious, I will not be categorical on that - the document states that the HVO is provoking, and it quotes a few examples such as the flag. You remember that the flag has caused some incidents afterwards. So what I'm interested in is the conclusion in the last paragraph. It states that the ECMM concludes that the provocation of the HVO is intense. This is what the document states. They may be right, they may be wrong, they may not have all the information required, but what I would like to know is: According to you, how did you see the situation? What do you say about that? And to clarify my question, it is obvious that this report is only dealing with the activities of the HVO, while they could also have looked into what was doing the ABiH, but they're not mentioning anything about that because perhaps on the other side the same thing was happening. But in this report, we're only dealing with the HVO. And, of course, this could give the relative value of this document. I would rather have a document that looks at the entirety of the situation, with all of its components, Serbs, Muslims, Croats, rather than a document looking only at one side of the story. So given that you were an analyst, what is your take on this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have already said, looking at the parts I read, because this is the first time that I'm seeing this document, it seems to me that this is the consequence of strong propaganda on the part of the BH Army, and that it was a follow-up to something that others attacked, and then they retaliated and took control of the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: I would like to ask also a question, and although our faces are sometimes watched, but I would like to ask the witness about the following matter. And actually it is Chapter 7 of the report, "The Present Analysis."

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No interpretation, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: So then I will repeat again. So I started saying that although sometimes our faces are watched, but nevertheless I make an attempt to ask a question from the witness, and it is about the last part of that report, chapter or part 7, "Present Analysis." And here it is being said that the -- in the third paragraph: "At the time of writing, the HVO are making their most serious attempt to isolate Jablanica before seizing it." And here I would like to ask the witness if, according to his knowledge as an analyst in VOS, how did he actually see the situation there as far as the HVO attempts, according to the report of the ECMM, that what kind of efforts have been made by the HVO, if any, to isolate Jablanica before its seizing? So it is my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it says here that the document is dated the 17th of April, that's what it says on the document, 1993. At that time, we know what we have in the Konjic-Jablanica region. We also know that large-scale activities on the part of the BH Army were underway for the first time on the 20th [as interpreted] of March, 1993, and then, following on from that, on the 13th of April, 1993, and that the ratio of forces -- the balance of forces at that time in the region was over 10:1 to the advantage of the BH Army. That's what we know for sure. We know that that's how things stood and that almost all the villages were under a blockade.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just to correct the transcript, the witness gave us the date. He said the 23rd of March, whereas the record says "the 20th of March." So "the first time on the 23rd of March 1993" is what we should read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, when I see a document coming from an international body, I do not always give it 100 per cent credibility or value: A judge in a criminal court of law looks at the various documents, compares documents, so I will not draw any conclusions from this document. Now, I look at the second paragraph in that chapter "Political Activity." Please look at this paragraph, second paragraph. In the first paragraph of this chapter, the observers say that the HVO is provoking. In the second paragraph -- and I don't understand why we changed that. Please go back to point 3, Registrar. I don't understand why we have moved. Let's go back to "Political Activities," please. There we go, Chapter 3, "Political Activity." Look at the way it's drafted. In the first paragraph, we talk about the clashes, and as a conclusion we say that it's provocation from the HVO. And then in the second paragraph, it says: "There is always a good story attached to any clash ..." And then it states that the Croatian media are talking about Mujahedin extremists, but, in fact, when this is written they do not know that Mujahedin extremists have committed crimes. It is not mentioned, it is just quoted as a proof or as a token of propaganda from the HVO, whereas in fact it is a fact, and this is why I'm very cautious when looking at those documents because documents have to be compared with everything else, and we should not only base any conclusions on one specific document. So as an analyst, I was wondering whether you knew that in part of the BiH there were Mujahedins who were causing problems. Were you aware of this, yes or no? Because according to European Observers, all this is false and has never existed, this is provocation, this is propaganda.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They knew that there were Mujahedin. We knew that there were Mujahedin in Bosnia and Herzegovina. And as far as this paragraph is concerned, let me try and explain. That was a very specific period. How come there is nothing else in the reports by the international community, UNPROFOR, and whoever was there, can be explained by this. After the 13th of April, UNPROFOR was forbidden to visit the Croatian enclaves in the territory of Konjic. The BiH Army did not allow them to enter those areas on the 13th of April and later on, including the 4th of May, when that meeting took place. They could not reach those areas or enter those areas, and I believe that that's why the report looks the way it does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're saying that after the 13th of April, UNPROFOR was banned from visiting any Croatian enclaves. If they did not go to those locations, they didn't have a clear view of the situation, which might explain these documents from the international community. Is that what you are wanting to tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, this is exactly what I meant to say. Conclusions were reached based on the information provided by the ABiH. They, themselves, could not inspect the area themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Kruger, perhaps we've made some progress.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I would like to, with your permission, add a question. Mr. Jasak, would you look at the last paragraph on that page, and the last paragraph of the chapter "Military Activity." Here the report says, and I quote: "The Muslims are not entirely blameless and have their own extremists, though for the most part made, not born. Observation and regular contact with the HVO suggests the presence of a hidden agenda." How do you interpret this? What does the term "hidden agenda" refer to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. I did not find where you were reading from. Could somebody tell me in Croatian? Could somebody refer me to the page in Croatian?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can say that this is page 3, last paragraph, above the title "Military Activities."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know what "hidden agenda" means here in this report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. It's a pity, because I don't know either. It can refer to the plans you have spoken of of the Muslims, but it can also refer to the HVO. I thought perhaps you had an idea. Thank you. Mr. Kruger.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Sir, Their Honours have dealt with most of the questions that I did want to ask you. Just before stepping off this document, if we look -- and this is the third section, "Political Activity," and it's the third paragraph of that section. It says: "Furthermore, the HVO have emphasised Muslim aggression." Now, sir, my question to you is: If I listen to you, you're also emphasising in your testimony Muslim aggression, but do you allow at all that it's possible that the Muslims were actually reacting to prior actions of the HVO? Isn't that possible?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the Muslims could be reacting to. And here that document was issued on the 17th of April, 1993. We know what the situation was at the time. I don't know who, in their right mind, could launch any activities against somebody who is tenfold stronger than them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: And to quickly return to the propaganda issue, did I understand you correctly that you said that the HVO was not involved in propaganda?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The HVO had its Information Service. However, the HVO never launched any such propaganda [realtime transcript read in error "proper today"] activities, nothing similar to what was done by the BiH Army. And they used the same procedures later on when they launched attacks. They pretended that they had come under attack by the enemy, which made them defend themselves, and then they took a large part of the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Page 27, line 3, it is recorded: "However, the HVO never launched any such proper today activities." The witness said, "The HVO never launched any propaganda activities." I think that it was obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Now, sir, let's explore a bit whether the HVO wasn't, indeed, doing anything which could have caused concern on the side of the Muslims. And for the first document, let's look at, and this is still binder 2, P0 -- sorry, P10926. It's about the eighth document from the end, 10926. Now, sir, this document purports to be an order from Mr. Mate Boban, dated the 10th of June, 1992, and it says: "Pursuant to the statutory decision on the provisional establishment of the executive authority and administration on the territory of the HZ-HB of 15 May 1992, I hereby order: "1. The establishment of the executive authority of the HVO in the Konjic municipality ..." Now, sir, were you aware that the HVO wished to establish its executive authority in the Konjic municipality?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of that. I don't know what that was about. At the time, I was the commander of a battalion in Mostar. I was not politically active.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. We have not seen this document before. This must be an excerpt from a book or a compilation of documents. I believe it would be fair from the Prosecution to explain the origin of the document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, when we tender the document or if we tender the document, we'll fully explain the origins and why we believe it can be admitted. But for cross-examination purposes, Your Honour, I think I'm fully entitled to put the document to the witness for a reaction.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I really have to react to this response by the Prosecutor. If Ms. Alaburic is going to prepare her re-examination, she needs to be familiar with the source of the document in order to test its probative value in her additional questions. This is the way I'm thinking, and I don't think that it is appropriate to answer an objection of this sort with such an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kruger, tell us where this document comes from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the full origins of the document are recorded in e-court, and it does, indeed, come from a book. And the page numbers of the book are also recorded there. It's in the book "Aggression on Bosnia and Genocide of Bosniaks" by Dr. Smail Cekic, 1991 to 1993, and it's pages 317 and 379, with reference to Annex 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Now, sir, this document clearly mentions the municipality, so isn't it so that the HVO wished to establish executive authority in all the municipalities which were being claimed for the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I've already said, as far as this document is concerned, at that time I was the commander of a battalion in Mostar. I don't know anything about the functioning of the civilian authorities. I don't know that there were any conflicts during that period of time. Any conflicts in the territory of Konjic up to the 23rd of March were daily affairs, and they were solved on a daily basis and never posed any problems. The problems arose only after that period: As far as I can see, this document was issued in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe the witness should give us the year together with the date that he mentioned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 23rd of March, 1993, that's when the conflicts started, and this document apparently was issued in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Let's move on to another document, then, three documents earlier in your binder, document P10919. 10919. Now, sir, this is a press release of the War Presidency of the Konjic Municipality, signed by Mr. Zejnil Delalic, who was the co-ordinator of the BH Army and War Presidency of Konjic Municipality. And in this public announcement from July 1992, he says: "Regarding the announcement of the Konjic HVO of 5 July 1992, filed under" reference number, "we are making the following announcement: "The Konjic HVO has surfaced as a self-proclaimed organisation allegedly in charge of supplying a complete range of products from Croatia. "This is not correct. Our municipality gets all its food and medical supplies, and oil and oil products, by buying them from bartering through the Economic Staff and business operators in Konjic military, or receiving them as a gift from domestic or international humanitarian aid organisations. The HVO does not take part in that. "On the contrary, the Konjic HVO interferes and obstructs the flow of these products obtained with great difficulty ..." Sir, do you know anything about the Muslims in Konjic viewing the HVO as being interfering and obstructive? And this was -- and this was 1992 that we're talking to July -- June 1992.

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that the HVO blocked anything. I've already told you that at that time I was the commander of a battalion in Mostar, and I know that we had excellent co-operation in the territory of Mostar when it came to the liberation of the city from the VRS. At the time, I was the commander of a battalion in Mostar. Therefore, I know nothing about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: So, sir, from what you've said with regard to this document and the previous one that I showed you, you don't know whether what is stated in those documents is true or not; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not even aware of the existence of the document, nor did I hear anything about any such things happening, so I can't really tell you anything. I've not -- I've never heard of anything that is referred to in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: But it is entirely possible -- because you don't know, it's possible that it's actually true, what's being stated in these documents, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you that. When a document of this sort is written, I don't know what the purpose of it may be. At the time, as I've already told you, I was in Mostar, I was the commander of a battalion, and I had excellent co-operation with the BiH Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, this sort of questioning, I suggest, is really -- unfairly confuses the witness, because witnesses come to answer questions and say what they know. They don't come to be asked to agree to simple propositions of logic, such as if they don't know anything about anything, then they can't say anything about that. So this is really a waste of time and confusing for a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may briefly respond to that. I would submit it's entirely appropriate, this line of questioning, because the whole point is the witness has expressed very categorical views on the ABiH being the aggressor and the HVO having done nothing to -- or not having been responsible for provocations or for the conflict. And the reason for putting this to the witness is simply to ascertain whether the witness really knew what he was talking about, and that's why I'm putting these documents to the witness. And if he knows nothing about them, then it makes a point.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, he said that. That's the point. At page 31, line 3: "I wasn't aware of the existence of the document, nor did I hear about any such things happening, so I can't really tell you anything." So end of story there. Now, if Mr. Kruger then wishes to challenge that and suggest that he does know something, or put something to him to say that he does know something, that's an entirely legitimate line of cross-examination, but not to go on, I submit, into these propositions of logic. It's really just argument, then, and that's not what witnesses come here for.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Your Honours -- my apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please. Mr. Kruger, you put your question, which was a very specific question, and you were entitled to do so. The witness answered your question and said that he could not answer your question because at the time he was not involved in this region, he was not there, and so on. On two occasions, you addressed the issue again, and on two occasions he answered likewise. You can waste your time and put the question a third time again, and he will answer in the same fashion.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your permission, I was just going to say something along the same lines as you, Your Honour Judge Antonetti. The witness said it clearly as to what he was able to know at the moment when he was the commander of a battalion in Mostar and what he was in a position to know after the month of October and further on when he was with the VOS and the Main Staff. I don't think that these two should be mixed and disqualify the answer pertaining to the time when he was a member of the VOS, because he was somewhere else before that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Well, sir, let's move, then, into October 1992, and let's have a look at document P00581. And this is still binder 2. This is the third document in your binder, sir. Now, sir, this document is a document that's already in evidence, Your Honours, from 15 October 1992, and it's by Zdravko Sagolj, the Herceg Stjepan Brigade commander, and it's to the Konjic Military Police, Jablanica Military Police, Klis Military Police, and a few other military police organisations. It says : "This is to inform you that as of 17 October 1992, all persons in the territory of Konjic and Jablanica that are in possession of a pass allowing them freedom of movement throughout the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and the Republic of Croatia shall have their passes authenticated with the Herceg Stjepan Brigade's stamp. "All persons in possession of passes that have been authenticated with any other stamp than that of Herceg Stjepan Brigade shall be invalid, and holder of any such pass shall not be permitted to enter and tour this territory." Now, just for the record, I note that the original document does refer in this instance to "teritorija." So, sir, were you aware of this order stating that only Herceg Stjepan Brigade stamps would be valid for travel passes?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order. I was not familiar with this. This had nothing to do with military intelligence, because this referred to the members of this brigade. It seems that the intention was not to allow anybody else to deal with the members of his brigade, or maybe something else. I really don't know. I've not seen this document before. In any case, this was not a military intelligence document. It is possible that he informs all the military police units that his men did not enough duty, he is inquiring whether anybody else had let them go. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Now, sir, but even though you haven't seen the document before, then, do you agree that on the face of it, this document says, in essence, that travel passes which would be issued by the RBiH and its authorities would not be valid? Isn't that what it implies?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. Objection, Your Honour, to the question. If the document had been read through, the reason would be obvious, the reason for the issuance of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Sir, can you answer? In essence, this would mean that travel documents issued by the authorities -- the legal authorities of the RBiH in Konjic and Jablanica would not be valid under certain circumstances?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't agree with that, absolutely not, because I can see a reference being made here to the area of Herceg-Bosna and the Republic of Croatia. The reason why this was issued was the abuse of stamps. Somebody must have stolen a stamp or something to that effect. But a local commander cannot put out of effect an existing agreement on co-operation between the Republic of Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina, which clearly demonstrates that the BiH Army and the HVO were both legal and legitimate. I don't see how a local commander could have an effect -- an influence on a pre-existing agreement. I don't see how he can allow somebody to move or not move around the territory of Herceg-Bosna. I don't know what the authorities of such a man would be, vis-à-vis everybody else, unless it is only vis-à-vis his own troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Sir, just before the break, perhaps: At that stage, October 1992, is it correct that all the municipalities which were identified to be part of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna actually formed part of the sovereign territory of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: All municipalities of Bosnia-Herzegovina are part of the sovereign territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina. That is very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: And according to this order, somebody from Konjic or from Jablanica who had a valid travel document issued by the authorities of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, according to this, they cannot travel into the areas being claimed for the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna; that pass would not be valid, isn't that what this says?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, I said that this was a local commander, and already at the time agreements existed on friendship and co-operation between Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Republic of Croatia. And I know that at that time people were travelling from Konjic and Mostar, people coming in, so I don't know of any such possibility that a commander of a local brigade could have any such influence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: All right, let's step off this topic. Your Honours, is it time for the break or we still have a few moments?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, it's time for the break, a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The court is back in session. Mr. Kruger, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Mr. Jasak, just before -- and continuing, it occurred to me that you went to the academy in Zagreb, the Military Academy, in 1993, and you remained there until 1994. Do you know, is that the same academy where General Petkovic at one stage was involved either as an instructor or had some role there?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I attended the Command Staff School, and General Petkovic appeared [as interpreted] as a lecturer there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: During the time when you were doing your --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise. The witness said General Petkovic was not a lecturer there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Petkovic did not appear during my schooling there as a lecturer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: During your period subsequently after the Command Staff School, from 1994 onwards, did you have anything to do with General Petkovic? Were you ever in the same units or working in the same sectors?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I had completed my schooling, yes, during a certain period of time. I think it was 1996 until 2000, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Yes. And what was the relationship between you and General Petkovic at that time, the professional relationship?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Petkovic was my commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Your immediate commander, and in which -- where were you working at that stage?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I was working in the Ston Military District, and General Petkovic was the commander of the Ston Military District, and I was head of the Department for Personnel and Legal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, sir, let's continue, and let's have a look at document P01139. This is two documents further on in the binder from where you are now. P01139. This document is already in evidence. This is a document from 15 January. It's an order signed by General Petkovic, and it is to the HVO and the BiH. Now, sir, this order, if we just read the preamble, it says: "Pursuant to the decision of the HZ-HB HVO ..." Before continuing, can you confirm or did you know what the HZ-HB HVO was?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. The HVO is the Croatian Defence Council, and the HZ-HB is the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Yes. And if there's reference to the Croatian Community of HVO decision, would that be the body of which Mr. Prlic was the president?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where your question is going, because from the memorandum -- or, rather, from the heading we can see it says "Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina," from the header, and then "the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna," and then "the Croatian Defence Council." That's the hierarchy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, let's move --

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then it goes on to say "HVO Main Headquarters" or "Main Staff."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Sorry. Witness, this was a very easy question. Did you know that Mr. Prlic was the president of this entity or not? It's a yes-or-no question, no comment called for.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't understand the question to be that, because at the time the president of the Croatian Defence Council was Mr. Prlic, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Well, that's the answer, then. The question is -- yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The civilian part.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, would you look at the question, and you'll see that the question wasn't put that way. And it's line 25, the question was "the Croatian Community of HVO," and that is why the witness did not understand what the question referred to, because the body that Mr. Prlic headed which was the HVO HZ-HB.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I didn't look at the literal formulation of the question, which I agree to you is puzzling, but I was looking at the document and what is set out on page 37, line 20. And that entity, I thought, was what the question referred to. Mr. Kruger.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That was indeed so and thank you for eliciting the answer or a response.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Now, sir, if we go on, it's pursuant to the decision, then, of the body of which Mr. Prlic was the head. And the order of the chief of the Defence Department, you agree that that is Mr. Stojic being referred to?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: " ... and pursuant to the Geneva Agreements on the structure of Bosnia and Herzegovina, as well as the jurisdiction of the Armed Forces Command in the provinces, I hereby order:" And then it says: "All units of the HVO Armed Forces and of the BH Army in Provinces 3, 8, 10," those are Croatian provinces, "be placed under the command of the HVO Main Headquarters, that is, under the command of the Central Bosnia, North-Western and South-Eastern Herzegovina Operative Zone." And if we continue to number 4, it says: "Members and units of the HVO Armed Forces and the BH Army who do not submit to the commands in items 1 and 2 herein leave the province where they do not belong; otherwise, they will be treated as paramilitary units and disarmed." Now, sir, my question to you is: You'll agree that this order relates to the implementation of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan; you don't disagree with that?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order relates to the provinces contained in the Vance-Owen Plan, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: And from paragraph 1, what this, in effect, says, if we look at those provinces, those provinces would include Konjic, for instance, and it says the units in Konjic municipality are to be placed under the command of the HVO Main Headquarters. And, furthermore, if those units in Konjic do not do this, and it says -- who do not submit to the commands, they must leave the province where they do not belong; otherwise, they will be treated as paramilitary units and disarmed. Now, sir, doesn't this mean that the ABiH in Konjic municipality, that majority of the soldiers - I think you mentioned the number of 14.000 - according to this, they must submit themselves to the command of the HVO, isn't that what this says, and if they don't, they have to leave?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, this order never came into force. It was never acted upon and implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: But, sir, this order -- that's not the question, whether it was implemented or acted upon. Does this mean that those soldiers -- ABiH soldiers in Konjic had to either submit to the HVO command or leave?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the order was not implemented, then they didn't have to be submitted to anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: We're not talking about the implementation yet. I'm talking about the practical implication. Does this order say, as it stands here, or imply, as it stands here, that those soldiers in Konjic, Muslim soldiers, ABiH, had to submit to the HVO or leave?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it didn't come into force, then they didn't have to become submitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Sir, if you look at paragraph 8, it says: "This order shall be carried out by 20 January 1993." Now, this order, if you place yourself in the shoes of the Muslims in Konjic, for instance, the ABiH in Konjic, certainly you would be very concerned about what the HVO is requiring of you; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge that this was sent to Konjic at all. That does not follow from this. It doesn't follow that it was sent to Konjic. But I say again I have no knowledge that this -- that any of the things contained in this order were ever carried out. And if we go back to this period, then there was another order at that time linked to the Vance-Owen Plan. Perhaps I could try and explain that general period. It was an order from the minister of defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina - his name was Bozo Rajic - and it related to all three components, and initially it meant a truce, a cessation of all hostilities. That's what it called for, and it had similar contents to this. So it meant the temporary de-blockade of Sarajevo and the withdrawal from areas where the Serbs were in the majority, where the Croats were in the majority, where the Muslims were in the majority, and so on. So this was something that was resorted to for that particular time so that they knew who was in command of what forces in the provinces, and then later on so that they could discuss overall demobilisation in Bosnia-Herzegovina. So the aim of that was an immediate cessation of conflicts, and the Croats saw the Vance-Owen Plan as a definite end to the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you say the Croats saw the Vance-Owen Plan as a definite end to the war, but certainly as an intelligence analyst you must have been aware that the Muslim side was not in favour of this Vance-Owen Peace Plan and they didn't agree with it. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Upon returning from Geneva, when our people working on that came back, the knowledge wasn't like that, because in January already it was agreed with Alija Izetbegovic that he would accept the Vance-Owen Plan and that he would sign it -- well, it was to have taken place in January, but there was some technicality involved. And I remember that I was personally given an assignment from General Petkovic to collect information about heavy artillery deployment for the entire HVO for that period and also the distribution of the minefields for the requirements of the negotiations in Geneva, and I was in charge of that personally. I drew those maps and so on. So that means that the goal was to locate where the artillery was located in order to prevent it from firing, and to draw up maps and exchange them on the layout of the minefields.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me put this to you: that the interpretation that the Bosnian Croats had of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan was not shared by the Muslims, the interpretation. They didn't agree with your interpretation. What would you say to that?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how they interpreted it. All I do know is that the Vance-Owen Plan was signed in its entirety in March 1993, and that, in principle, they had agreed on all the points as early on as January 1993. So if something was signed and a document existed, and you had a map, then I think that's it, that's the end of the story. As far as interpretations go, it is only the international community that can interpret things, because it was under its auspices that it was carried through.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Sir, let's move on from this, and let's move to March 1993. And I refer you to document 4D00454. This is the second-last document in your binder. This document is already in evidence. Now, sir, the document you have before you is dated the 20th of March, 1993, and it's a protocol of the joint meeting of representatives of the RBiH Army, commands and representatives of RBiH Ministry of Interior, and the meeting was held on 20 March. The subject of this meeting, we see just below "Protocol," it says -- at least "subject," you will see just below the "Protocol," "Subject" is: "The assessment of military-safety situation in the area of Hadzici, Jablanica, Konjic municipalities with regard to the Croatian Defence Council." And then it starts off with saying: "Upon analysis of the military-safety situation in the free territories of the indicated municipalities, significant deterioration of the relations between HVO and legal government authorities of the RBiH and the Army of RBiH in the recent period, and particularly since continued negotiations in New York began, was established. The reasons thereof lie in the establishment by force of parallel authorities by HVO, which is manifested through:" And then various instances of manifestation of this attempt to establish parallel authorities is listed. Now, sir, I put it to you that the HVO was, indeed, trying to establish parallel authorities in various municipalities, including Konjic and Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any knowledge of any establishment of parallel authority in the Konjic-Jablanica area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: And the legal authorities in Konjic and Jablanica, the authorities of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, they were concerned about the actions of the HVO? Do you allow for that, that this could be a reason why later on, a month later, Mr. Halilovic asks Mr. Petkovic, Are we still friends, or Are we allies or enemies?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to do any guess-work here. When you mention legal organs, legal authorities, absolutely the HVO was a legal, and I think we've established that already in the previous days, so I don't see how the problem of legality crops up here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: But those authorities were being interfered with or worked against by the HVO. The HVO was usurping their power, isn't that so, and their authority?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could we have an example of how, in Jablanica, for instance, when you had the doctor who was appointed by Izetbegovic to take over that region, how is it that -- and in what concrete fashion did the HVO in Jablanica or Konjic actually took over authority? And if he can prove that and show that, then he can pose that question. That's the predicate, as opposed to just hypothesising in the air, like a feather in a storm.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I might remind you that the topic of civilian authorities were not covered in the examination-in-chief, and, therefore, I think that Mr. Kruger should refrain from posing leading questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may respond to that. The summary makes it very clear that the witness testifies that the position in Konjic Municipality is that it was the ABiH which precipitated the conflict, they were responsible for it. These questions go directly to that topic, because they are designed to indicate that this simply is not so, and the HVO, be it the military or the civilian authorities, had a very big role in provoking that conflict. And that's why this falls squarely within the ambit of cross-examination, Your Honour, I submit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once again, these are objections that are wasting our time. You have heard the Prosecutor. He's talking about provocations from the HVO, and do you agree or don't you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't agree about these HVO provocations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, he doesn't agree, so please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Now, sir, let's move to the actual attack in Konjic, the ABiH attack, on the 23rd of March, 1993. Now, your testimony, as I understand it, is that on the 23rd of March, it's 1993, it's the ABiH which launched this attack, and it was entirely unprovoked by any actions from the HVO side. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Let's have a look at document P01747. 1747. Now, sir, this document is an --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Would that document be protected? It says "Confidential" on the first page, and it's a SpaBat document, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is one of those documents where we are allowed to talk about it, as long as we don't broadcast it, an image of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: It's good to know that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, and thank you for alerting me to that. I missed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Now, sir, this document is an UNPROFOR report from UNPROFOR Kiseljak to UNPROFOR Headquarters Zagreb, and it's a weekly information summary for the period 22 to 28 March. And we only have the translation of the portions that I'm going to put to you, and the first part I'm putting to you -- want to show you is paragraph 4(b), which is on page 3 of 8 in the English version. And 4 is the report for the BritBat Sector. 4(b) relates to Gornji Vakuf, and it says: "The relationship between the Muslims and the Croats appears to have deteriorated during the past seven days. On 21 March, according to BritBat reports, the HVO to the east of Prozor attacked the Muslim village of Here. Following this attack, concentration of soldiers from both sides were noted in the surrounding villages." Sir, are you aware or is that correct that on the 21st of March the HVO attacked the village of Here?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: But, sir, as an analyst, certainly if this is true, then certainly this may or would have an impact on how the ABiH viewed their security in neighbouring areas; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've said a number of times that the HVO had less men, and in case of any attacks it was clear what would happen, what the outcome would have been. So I don't have any knowledge to the effect that the HVO attacked anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Sir, the fact that you don't know about this is just because you weren't privy to all information regarding the HVO activities, even though you were in the Main Staff; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I was informed of the enemy activities in these parts, and so, according to the reports we had, there were no conflicts, which means that the HVO did not cause the conflicts, provoke the conflicts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Sir, I put it to you that if we look at the ABiH attack in Konjic, we simply cannot evaluate that attack on the 23rd of March, 1993, without taking into account this attack by the HVO in Prozor two days earlier.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, let us just be more precise. It wasn't about the attack in Prozor that was referred to, but the village of Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: I'll reformulate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Sir, the attack of the ABiH in Konjic on the 23rd of March, 1993, we cannot evaluate or judge what happened there without taking into account the HVO attack in the village of Here, which is in the municipality of Prozor, two days earlier; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
